gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-adlam-un: Laser-cut sheet metal comes to mind, with Quantum's loose letterfit and single stroke width up top. And Noto Sans Adlam Unjoined matches that openness with generous gaps between curve ends and stems.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-armenian: A flat gray hum of lines, loosely spaced. Shrink Quantum and that constant line weight fades, whereas Noto Sans Armenian holds up with full-standing c, s and z and wide, inviting round letters.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-bassa-va: Noto Sans Bassa Vah lets its dominant midsection swallow the line's height, with a pliers-jawed c. And Quantum does best with loose spacing and cord-like strokes, while the body font does best with that heavy midsection.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-bengali: Ink poured at a single width is Quantum's whole look, loosely spaced and open-mouthed. Noto Sans Bengali does the other half, with distinctly open letter mouths and capitals hugging lowercase height.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-bhaiksuk: Clean, uniform strokes with zero contrast, spaced loosely, lead the way in Quantum. Noto Sans Bhaiksuki then brings swollen, rope-coiled lowercase and open apertures, which keep paragraphs comfortably readable.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-chakma: Quantum runs one uninterrupted line width through every letter, loosely spaced, while Noto Sans Chakma packs its lowercase up toward the caps. Big and brief is where Quantum looks best.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-cham: A pen line that holds one width throughout defines Quantum, loosely spaced and open. Noto Sans Cham matches it with rounded, lofty lowercase and c openings with plenty of entry space, an openness both fonts share.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-cherokee: Quantum leaves the single-width trail of a rolling-ball pen, loosely spaced, with mouths that stay open and ascenders cut short. Noto Sans Cherokee gives paragraphs a deep band and a wide-gapped e.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-cuneifor: Lowercase swollen like inflated glass beads, with an e that opens rather than closing its eye, reads freely. Noto Sans Cuneiform has that, while Quantum, with its drafting-pen outline look, is best big and short.
gen-dafont-quantum-gf-noto-sans-devanaga: Quantum does best as a monoline, loosely spaced face, stem to serif, with open mouths. And Noto Sans Devanagari is best at compactness, its capitals blending into lowercase and its g left open below.
